findings.failure_mode: malformed file path or unreadable file aborts the entire program with a panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error type) and propagate with ? or explicit map_err

findings.failure_mode: non-numeric or out-of-range value in the second CSV field panics instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError::BadValue(...)) and propagate, or return Result

findings.problem: lossy `as u16` cast after parse — integer width cast
findings.failure_mode: values that parsed successfully as u32 but exceed u16::MAX silently wrap to a wrong value instead of being rejected
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 using `parse::<u16>()` or use `u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err()`

findings.problem: split(',') + collect + indexed access instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: allocates a full Vec of Strings for every line; if the line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, parts[0] and parts[1] indexing panics at runtime
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest), then rest.split_once(',') to get the value field; handle None cases with map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect in data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: parsing/presentation coupling makes the function non-deterministic, untestable in isolation, and violates the functional core / imperative shell boundary
findings.fix: move println! to the shell layer that consumes the Vec<Record>; the core parser should return data only with no side effects

findings.problem: load_sessions performs I/O (fs::read_to_string) — mixing imperative shell and functional core
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without a real file; the function couples file system access to domain record construction
findings.fix: split into `fn load_sessions_from(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error>` (shell) that calls `fn parse_sessions(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>` (pure core)

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no domain validation by construction
findings.failure_mode: any string (empty, whitespace-only) and any u16 value is accepted, including values that are semantically invalid in the domain
findings.fix: wrap name in a `UserName` newtype with a fallible constructor; use a domain error enum for invalid records instead of allowing illegal states

findings.problem: Allocating Vec<String> and cloning each part unnecessarily — intermediate allocations in pure pipeline
findings.failure_mode: each line allocates a Vec and multiple Strings; for large files this causes excessive heap pressure and GC pressure
findings.fix: use split_once to borrow &str segments from the line without cloning; only allocate the final Record fields

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() — unnecessary String clone from collected Vec
findings.failure_mode: redundant allocation per record; the string was already cloned into the Vec during collect()
findings.fix: after split_once, use the &str directly: Record { name: name_part.to_string(), ... } — only one allocation per field
